question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
Yes. Electricity inflation is running well ahead of overall inflation, though the gap has narrowed a lot.

**Latest month (August 2026, annual change)**
- Electricity: +13.2%
- All groups CPI: +4.0%
- Electricity is about 9 percentage points higher.

**Recent path of the gap**

| Month | Electricity | All groups CPI |
|---|---|---|
| Oct 2025 | +37.1% | +3.8% |
| Feb 2026 | +37.0% | +3.7% |
| Jun 2026 | +22.4% | +3.8% |
| Jul 2026 | +6.1% | +3.5% |
| Aug 2026 | +13.2% | +4.0% |

- **Earlier in 2025:** Electricity prices were falling year on year, by 5.9% to 13.2% from January to June 2025. They then jumped to +13.6% in July 2025 and reached +37.1% by October 2025.
- **Since then:** Electricity has stayed above 20% through June 2026. It dropped to +6.1% in July 2026 and rebounded to +13.2% in August.
- **Why the pattern:** Annual changes this large usually reflect base effects. The 2025 rebate rollout and its timing lowered the base, and later changes in rebates and tariffs moved it again. I haven't checked this against the underlying data.
- **Headline CPI:** It has crept up from 1.9% in June 2025 to 4.0% in August 2026. Its peak so far was 4.6% in March 2026.

Electricity has been above headline inflation every month since July 2025, and it is still well above it. The July 2026 dip to 6.1% was the smallest gap in that period, and August widened it again. The monthly figures are volatile, so I'd read the trend over several months rather than any one reading.
